title: ME02a: Beyond the Bullshit - The Self-Help Trap
author: Richard Claydon
summary: Claydon tells the story of Maya, a diligent leadership-development graduate, to argue that individual self-improvement frameworks fail when the surrounding system contradicts them. Type profiles, strengths, purpose statements, growth mindset, grit and virtue-based models each worked for a while and then collapsed against incoherent structures, unclear decision rights and cultures that punished vulnerability. Drawing on Pfeffer's Leadership BS and Frankfurt's On Bullshit, he reframes her burnout as betrayal by a leadership industry that blames the leader rather than the system. The essay's move is to redirect attention from traits to role, context and system. It closes with self-, role- and system-reflection questions.
points: Leadership tools like type profiles and strengths frameworks lose value when the system gives a leader no decision rights and conflicting reporting lines.
Grit is recast as a trap: it correlates with staying too long in roles that quietly break conscientious people, rather than with success.
Virtue-based models such as authenticity and servant leadership become risky when the culture rewards speed, spin and sacrifice.
Pfeffer and Frankfurt supply the diagnosis that the industry sells inspiration while rewarding obedience and politics.
The author concludes that leadership is a performance inside a system, so development must turn outward toward role and structure.
quotes: Suddenly, her type didn’t help her navigate three reporting lines and zero decision rights. Her “strengths” contradicted each other by project.
Eventually, “growth mindset” started to feel less like empowerment and more like gaslighting.
Grit didn’t correlate with success. It correlated with staying too long in roles that were quietly breaking them. It was the conscientious ones who suffered most.
Until she noticed something chilling. The more virtuous she became, the more exposed she felt.
Bullshit, he argued, isn’t a lie. It’s a performance of meaning that doesn’t care if it’s true.

Because leadership isn’t a personality. It’s a performance inside a system. And no matter how pure your mindset, no matter how brave your purpose, no matter how authentic your heart, if the system punishes the very things it praises, the problem isn’t you.
